Our Story

From Backyard to Community Table

What started as a personal mission to understand where our food comes from has grown into something bigger. Noongu Farms is our backyard operation in Suwanee, GA — a living experiment in organic, sustainable growing guided by UGA Extension principles.

We grow over 43 varieties of vegetables, herbs, fruits, and rhizomes across 7 distinct zones. More than what we grow, we're focused on how we grow — sharing every lesson, failure, and victory with a community of beginner farmers who deserve real support.

  • Organic first — no synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, ever
  • Transparent documentation — we share our real journey, not just the wins
  • Community over competition — helping beginners is our core mission
  • UGA Extension–guided practices for Georgia Zone 8a
What We Grow

Our Star Crops

Six focus areas define the heart of Noongu Farms — each fully documented so you can grow them too.

🌳

Moringa

The miracle drumstick tree — one of the most nutrient-dense plants on earth. Started in our greenhouse for a head start, then transplanted outdoors. Fast-growing, generous, and deeply satisfying. Every leaf, pod, and seed documented.

Greenhouse → Zone FYear-round
🌾

Turmeric & Ginger

Our golden rhizomes — planted April 8 in rich grow bags, harvested November–December after 8–10 months. Chemical-free and full of the deep orange colour that signals real quality. We share the full method.

Grow BagApr – Dec
🐔

Fresh Eggs

Four happy hens providing fresh eggs year-round and teaching us about integrated farm ecosystems. Part of the family, contributors to our compost, and key to our soil health philosophy.

Free rangeYear-round
🍅

Tomatoes & Peppers

Zone D is our flavour powerhouse — Large Red Cherry, Roma, Aunt Molly's Cherry, Shishito, King of North, Jalapeno Orange Spice, Banana Peppers, and Big Thai Hot. Seeds started Feb 8. Harvest June through October.

Zone DJun – Oct
🫐

Berries & Fruits

Strawberries in Zone B (May–Jun), Raspberries in Zone A (Jun–Aug), three new Blueberry bushes in Zone E (Jun–Aug), and a mature Pomegranate (Sep–Nov). Four zones, five months of fresh fruit.

Zones A · B · EMay – Nov
🥒

Cucurbits & Zone F

Our most diverse zone — Beit Alpha and Jibai cucumbers, Madhu Ras melon, sweet corn, Amsterdam celery, Chinese Red Noodle Beans climbing 6 feet, Hyacinth Bean, and a banana plant beginning its long journey.

Zone FApr – Oct

Carrots / Root crops

A Weekly Apr–Jun
Key insect pests

Carrot rust fly, Wireworm, Nematodes

Key diseases

Alternaria blight, Cavity spot

Organic prevention

Row cover at sow; 3-yr rotation; avoid carrot-family 3 yrs

Organic treatment

Beneficial nematodes; kaolin clay; pyrethrin spray

Lettuce / Leafy greens

A 2× weekly Mar–Jun
Key insect pests

Aphids, Slugs, Leaf miners, Cutworms

Key diseases

Downy mildew, Bottom rot, Tip burn

Organic prevention

Row cover; drip irrigation; diatomaceous earth for slugs

Organic treatment

Neem oil; iron phosphate bait; spinosad for leaf miners

Raspberries

A Weekly Jun–Aug
Key insect pests

Japanese beetle, Aphids, Spider mite, Cane borer

Key diseases

Botrytis, Cane blight, Anthracnose

Organic prevention

Remove spent canes; dormant oil Feb; neem spray spring

Organic treatment

Copper fungicide; neem for mites; hand-pick beetles

Strawberries

B Every 2 days at peak
Key insect pests

Slugs, Spider mite, Strawberry weevil, SWD

Key diseases

Gray mold (Botrytis), Leaf scorch, Anthracnose

Organic prevention

Straw mulch; row cover; drip irrigation; remove debris

Organic treatment

Neem oil; copper spray; remove infected berries immediately

Brassicas (Cauliflower, Cabbage, Brussels)

C Weekly Apr–Jul
Key insect pests

Cabbage looper, Cabbageworm, Aphids, Harlequin bug

Key diseases

Black rot, Downy mildew, Clubroot, Alternaria

Organic prevention

Row cover at transplant; 3-yr rotation; remove debris

Organic treatment

Bt for loopers/worms; neem oil; sticky traps

Alliums (Spring Onions)

C Weekly Apr–Jun
Key insect pests

Thrips, Onion maggot, Nematodes

Key diseases

Downy mildew, Fusarium basal rot

Organic prevention

3-yr rotation; avoid alliums 3 yrs; raised beds for drainage

Organic treatment

Spinosad for thrips; beneficial nematodes for maggot

Legumes (Beans, Peas, Noodle Beans)

C/F Every 3 days Jun–Aug
Key insect pests

Mexican bean beetle, Spider mite, Aphids

Key diseases

Bean rust, Mosaic virus, Angular leaf spot

Organic prevention

2-yr rotation; avoid wetting foliage; resistant varieties

Organic treatment

Neem oil; insecticidal soap; remove virus-infected plants

Solanaceae (Tomatoes, Peppers, Eggplant)

D 2× weekly May–Oct
Key insect pests

Hornworm, Fruitworm, Aphids, Whitefly, Stinkbug, Flea beetle

Key diseases

Early blight, Septoria, Late blight, BER, Fusarium wilt

Organic prevention

Stake; mulch 3"; drip irrigation; copper spray preventive

Organic treatment

Bt for hornworm; neem oil; kaolin clay; calcium spray for BER

Perennial fruits (Blueberry, Pomegranate)

E Weekly May–Oct
Key insect pests

SWD, Blueberry maggot, Aphids, Scale, Birds

Key diseases

Mummy berry, Botrytis, Alternaria, Crown gall

Organic prevention

Bird netting at fruit set; dormant oil Feb; pine bark mulch

Organic treatment

Neem oil; copper for fungal; remove mummified berries

Cucurbits (Cucumber, Melon, Corn)

F Every 3 days May–Aug
Key insect pests

Cucumber beetle, Spider mite, Aphids, Corn earworm

Key diseases

Powdery mildew, Downy mildew, Fusarium wilt

Organic prevention

Trellis for airflow; drip; row cover; 3-yr rotation

Organic treatment

Neem oil; Bt for earworm; kaolin clay; sulfur for PM

Moringa

GH/F Monthly
Key insect pests

Aphids, Whitefly, Caterpillars

Key diseases

Leaf spot, Root rot (if overwatered)

Organic prevention

Good drainage; avoid overwatering; neem oil preventive

Organic treatment

Neem oil spray; insecticidal soap for aphids/whitefly

Rhizomes (Ginger, Turmeric)

GrowBag Monthly Apr–Nov
Key insect pests

Root knot nematode, Rhizome fly, Soft rot bacteria

Key diseases

Rhizome rot, Pythium, Fusarium, Leaf blotch

Organic prevention

Well-draining grow bag; avoid waterlogging; mulch surface

Organic treatment

Beneficial nematodes; remove rotted rhizomes; copper fungicide

Okra (Greenhouse)

GH Every 3 days Jun–Oct
Key insect pests

Aphids, Corn earworm, Stinkbug, Whitefly

Key diseases

Fusarium wilt, Root knot nematode, Powdery mildew

Organic prevention

Harvest frequently; good GH ventilation; drip irrigation

Organic treatment

Neem oil; Bt for earworm; yellow sticky traps

Herbs / Pots

Pot Monthly / when watering
Key insect pests

Aphids, Mealybug, Spider mite

Key diseases

Root rot, Powdery mildew, Damping off

Organic prevention

Excellent drainage; avoid overwatering; good air circulation

Organic treatment

Neem oil; insecticidal soap; repot if root rot

Meet the Farmer

The Human Behind the Harvest

G-Ni
Founder · Noongu Farms · Suwanee, GA

I'm a backyard farmer in Suwanee, Georgia growing 43 varieties of vegetables, fruits, herbs, and rhizomes across a carefully planned Zone 8a plot. What started as curiosity became a mission: prove organic growing is achievable for anyone, document the journey honestly, and build a community where beginners feel genuinely welcome.

I follow UGA Extension principles, practice IPM pest management, and work through a detailed 2026 Master Crop Plan. Everything I learn, I share here. Every mistake becomes a post. Every harvest is a celebration for all of us.
